words.english_meaning: Happening or done without prior planning, on a sudden natural impulse.
words.gujarati_meaning: pehela-thi-aayojan-vagar — achaanek-j-mun-thayu ane nikli-pddya — tatkalik-no-anubhav.
words.usage_note: Often used positively to describe outings that turned out wonderfully despite zero planning.
words.memory_tip: 'Spontaneous' = achaanek-no vichar → spontaneous picnic = 'Chalo, aajej jaiyu!' — pehela-na-plan-vagar.
examples: The spontaneous picnic after the morning market was the best part of the trip.
She loved spontaneous outings — they always turned out to be the most fun.
It was a completely spontaneous decision to drive to the countryside that afternoon.
Some of the most memorable days are the spontaneous ones.

words.english_meaning: Describing an activity or experience that is good, healthy, and morally positive — leaving you feeling complete.
words.gujarati_meaning: aw-pramaanik ane swasthya-purna anubhav — je man-ane-tan-ne-saro-feel-karaave.
words.usage_note: Used to describe activities that are good for the spirit and bring families or friends together positively.
examples: A family picnic is the most wholesome way to spend a weekend afternoon.
There is something deeply wholesome about eating food you cooked yourself outdoors.
The children's laughter made the whole outing feel truly wholesome.
She described the weekend trip to the countryside as wholesome and restorative.

words.english_meaning: Describing a place or situation that is extremely peaceful, beautiful, and ideally suited to happiness.
words.gujarati_meaning: aw-jaga ya parithiti je bilkul-shaant, sundar ane aanand-maate-made-for — swarg-jaisi.
words.usage_note: A higher-register word; used in travel writing and personal essays to describe a perfect, almost dreamlike setting.
words.memory_tip: 'Idyllic' = swarg-jaisi sundarata → idyllic picnic spot = jyaa jaao to din-yadgaar bani jaay.
examples: The orchard in bloom was an idyllic setting for their anniversary picnic.
She described the afternoon as idyllic — warm sun, good food, and great company.
Finding an idyllic spot by the stream made all the planning worthwhile.
The waterfront at golden hour was nothing short of idyllic.

words.english_meaning: Describing a warm, friendly, and lively atmosphere created by people enjoying each other's company.
words.gujarati_meaning: aw-garm ane maitripoorn vataavaran — jyaa log ek-bee-sathe aanandthi-bethe-hoi — dosti-no aanand.
words.usage_note: A slightly formal adjective; commonly found in restaurant and event reviews.
words.memory_tip: 'Con' = saath + 'vivial' = jeevant → convivial = saath-maa-jeevant ane mast — dosti-bhari masti.
examples: The picnic had a wonderfully convivial atmosphere — everyone was relaxed and laughing.
Good food and open air always create a convivial mood.
The convivial gathering stretched well into the evening.
There is nothing like a potluck picnic to generate a truly convivial spirit.

words.english_meaning: Describing something that makes you feel energetic, alert, and full of life.
words.gujarati_meaning: aw-anubhav jo urja ane chalakpan aape — tan-man-ne-uthaan-aave — fresh feeling.
words.usage_note: Often collocates with fresh air, cold water, or a brisk walk — all common elements of outdoor outings.
words.memory_tip: 'Invigorate' = urja bharo → invigorating = aw-kriya je tanmanma-navi-urja-bhere — fresh feel.
examples: The brisk nature walk before breakfast was invigorating for everyone.
Cold fresh air from the hills felt deeply invigorating after the city's pollution.
She found the paddling in the stream surprisingly invigorating.
An invigorating morning outdoors sets a positive tone for the whole day.

words.english_meaning: Moving or proceeding calmly without rush or pressure, allowing time to enjoy each moment fully.
words.gujarati_meaning: aw-jaldi-vagar — aaraampurvak — drek-pal-maanvanu — koi-pressure-vagar-shaant-reetho.
words.usage_note: A picnic done at an unhurried pace is considered the ideal — no agenda, no clock-watching.
examples: They spent an unhurried afternoon at the waterfront, with nowhere to be.
The best picnics are unhurried — you eat when you're hungry and leave when you're ready.
She loved the unhurried pace of their countryside outing.
An unhurried morning walk before the picnic set a perfectly relaxed tone.

words.english_meaning: Deeply absorbed in and surrounded by the natural environment, feeling completely at one with the outdoors.
words.gujarati_meaning: prakruti-maa-tamam ane poora-j-dubhu — sheher-bhulayelu — ane prakruti-sathe-ekroop thayelu.
words.usage_note: Used to express a profound connection with the natural environment rather than simply being outdoors.
words.memory_tip: 'Immersed' = dubhu → immersed in nature = prakruti-maa-pooro-dubhu — sheher bhulayelu.
examples: Spending a whole day in the forest left her feeling completely immersed in nature.
The children were so immersed in nature that they forgot about their phones entirely.
Being immersed in nature for even one day can dramatically reduce stress levels.
The best picnics leave you feeling truly immersed in nature rather than just visiting it.

mini_dialogues.title: Planning the picnic
mini_dialogues.situation: Two friends plan a weekend outing.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Shall we go on a picnic this weekend?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Yes! Let's plan a day trip to the meadow on the riverbank.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'll prepare the itinerary and pack the hamper.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Great — let's make the most of the good weather.

mini_dialogues.title: Choosing a spot
mini_dialogues.situation: You arrive and look for the perfect place to settle.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Where should we set up?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Let's find some shade — it's scorching today.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: There's a lovely clearing near that grove of trees.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Perfect. Spread the picnic rug there.

mini_dialogues.title: Talking about the weather
mini_dialogues.situation: You check the sky during the picnic.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: The sky looks a bit overcast.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: There's a cool breeze too — quite pleasant, actually.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: As long as it doesn't drizzle.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Even if it does, we'll just lounge under the umbrella.

mini_dialogues.title: Enjoying the moment
mini_dialogues.situation: You relax and admire the view.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: This is such a laid-back afternoon.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: I know — eating in the open air is the best.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: The view across the valley is breathtaking.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Definitely a picture-perfect spot.

mini_dialogues.title: Wrapping up
mini_dialogues.situation: The outing is ending and you pack up.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Should we pack up the leftovers?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Yes, and let's bin the disposable plates.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Want to take a stroll before we head back?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Sure — a little wander along the trail sounds nice. I really needed this change of scenery.

quiz.title: Picnic / Outing (Intermediate-Advanced) — Self-Test Quiz
quiz.instructions: Choose the correct option. Questions test meaning (English<->Gujarati), fill-in-the-blank, synonyms, antonyms, and definitions.

questions.question: What is the Gujarati meaning of 'Hamper'?
Which word is closest in meaning to 'Stroll'?
It's scorching — let's sit in the ____.
Which word means 'ઘાસ અને ફૂલોવાળું ખુલ્લું મેદાન'?
What is the opposite of 'Scorching'?
A 'day trip' is best described as:
options: A journey there and back in the same day
A trip with several overnight stays
questions.answer: A journey there and back in the same day

questions.question: Which word can replace 'Unwind'?
What is the Gujarati meaning of 'Overcast'?
The guide handed us the day's ____.
Which word means 'ઝરમર / હળવો વરસાદ'?
Let's ____ this sunny day and head outdoors.
What is the opposite of 'Pleasant'?
What is the Gujarati meaning of 'Breathtaking'?
We grilled chicken on the ____ in the garden.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'Laid-back'?

words.english_meaning: Salty or spicy in taste, rather than sweet.
words.gujarati_meaning: મીઠું/તીખું (ગળ્યું નહિ) સ્વાદવાળું.
words.usage_note: Opposite of 'sweet'; e.g. samosas are savoury. (US spelling: 'savory'.)
examples: I prefer savoury snacks to sweets.
She made a savoury pie for dinner.
The menu has both sweet and savoury options.
These crackers have a nice savoury flavour.

words.english_meaning: Having little or no strong flavour.
words.gujarati_meaning: સ્વાદ વગરનું, ફિક્કું.
words.usage_note: Negative for taste; food that needs more seasoning.
examples: The soup was bland and needed salt.
Hospital food can be quite bland.
He found the curry too bland.
Add some spices so it isn't bland.

words.english_meaning: Having a strong, sharp, pleasant taste, often sour or citrusy.
words.gujarati_meaning: તીખાશભર્યો, ખટમધુરો સ્વાદ.
words.usage_note: Pleasantly sharp — like lemon, tamarind, or yoghurt.
examples: The tangy lemon dressing was delicious.
I love the tangy taste of tamarind.
The sauce had a nice tangy kick.
Yoghurt gives the dish a tangy flavour.

words.english_meaning: Looking or smelling so delicious that it makes you want to eat it.
words.gujarati_meaning: મોઢામાં પાણી લાવી દે એવું સ્વાદિષ્ટ.
words.usage_note: Strong positive for how food looks or smells.
examples: The mouth-watering smell of biryani filled the house.
The menu had a mouth-watering selection.
She showed me a mouth-watering photo of the cake.
Those sweets look absolutely mouth-watering.

words.english_meaning: (Of food) containing a lot of fat, cream, sugar, or spices; heavy.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઘી/ક્રીમ/ખાંડથી ભરપૂર, ભારે.
words.usage_note: Here 'rich' means heavy/indulgent food, not money.
examples: The chocolate cake was very rich.
This gravy is rich and creamy.
A rich meal can feel heavy.
The dessert was too rich for me.

words.english_meaning: No longer fresh, especially of bread or other food.
words.gujarati_meaning: વાસી, તાજું ન રહેલું.
words.usage_note: 'Go stale' = become old/dry. Opposite of 'fresh'.
examples: The bread had gone stale.
Don't eat those stale biscuits.
Stale food can upset your stomach.
The cake tasted stale after a week.

words.english_meaning: Having a fresh, lively, often citrus-like flavour.
words.gujarati_meaning: તાજગીભર્યો, લીંબુ જેવો ચટપટો સ્વાદ.
words.usage_note: Suggests bright, refreshing flavour (often lemon/lime). 'Zest' = citrus peel.
examples: The salad had a zesty lime dressing.
I added orange zest for a zesty taste.
It's a light, zesty summer drink.
The marinade gives the fish a zesty flavour.

words.english_meaning: To cook gently in liquid just below boiling point.
words.gujarati_meaning: ધીમા તાપે ઉકાળવું (ઉકળતા પહેલાંના તાપે).
words.usage_note: Slow, gentle cooking with small bubbles, not a rolling boil.
examples: Let the curry simmer for twenty minutes.
Simmer the sauce gently until it thickens.
The soup simmered on the stove.
Reduce the heat and let it simmer.

words.english_meaning: To fry food quickly in a small amount of hot fat or oil.
words.gujarati_meaning: થોડા તેલમાં ઝડપથી તળવું / સાંતળવું.
words.usage_note: Quick frying over high heat. (French; said 'SOH-tay'.)
examples: Sauté the onions until golden.
She sautéed the vegetables in butter.
Lightly sauté the garlic first.
The mushrooms were sautéed to perfection.

words.english_meaning: To soak food in a seasoned liquid before cooking to add flavour.
words.gujarati_meaning: મસાલાવાળા પ્રવાહીમાં પલાળી રાખવું.
words.usage_note: The liquid itself is the 'marinade'. Adds flavour and tenderness.
examples: Marinate the chicken overnight for best flavour.
We marinated the paneer in spices.
The meat needs to marinate for an hour.
She marinated the fish in lemon and herbs.

words.english_meaning: To beat eggs, cream, or a mixture quickly to add air.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઝડપથી ફીણવું / ફેંટવું (ઈંડા/ક્રીમ).
words.usage_note: Both a verb and the wire tool used for it.
examples: Whisk the eggs until fluffy.
Whisk the batter to remove lumps.
She whisked the cream into soft peaks.
Whisk together the flour and milk.

words.english_meaning: To press and stretch dough with your hands until smooth.
words.gujarati_meaning: લોટ/કણક હાથથી મસળવું.
words.usage_note: The 'k' is silent — said 'need'. Essential for bread/roti dough.
examples: Knead the dough for ten minutes.
She kneaded the flour into a soft dough.
Keep kneading until it's smooth.
Well-kneaded dough makes soft rotis.

words.english_meaning: To add salt, pepper, or spices to food to improve its flavour.
words.gujarati_meaning: મીઠું-મસાલા ઉમેરવા.
words.usage_note: 'Season to taste' = add as much as you like. Noun 'seasoning' = the spices.
examples: Season the soup with salt and pepper.
Don't forget to season the rice.
Season to taste before serving.
She seasoned the curry generously.

words.english_meaning: To decorate food with a small amount of something to make it look attractive.
words.gujarati_meaning: સજાવટ માટે ઉપર પાથરવું / શણગારવું.
words.usage_note: Both a verb and a noun (the decoration itself).
examples: Garnish the dish with fresh coriander.
She garnished the soup with cream.
A garnish of lemon adds colour.
The chef garnished the plate with herbs.

words.english_meaning: A style or method of cooking, especially of a particular country or region.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ પ્રદેશ/સંસ્કૃતિની રસોઈ-શૈલી.
words.usage_note: Refers to a cooking tradition. (French; said 'kwi-ZEEN'.)
examples: I love Italian cuisine.
The restaurant serves South Indian cuisine.
We tried the local cuisine on holiday.
Thai cuisine is known for its bold flavours.

words.english_meaning: A small dish served before the main course to start a meal.
words.gujarati_meaning: મુખ્ય ભોજન પહેલાંની હળવી વાનગી / સ્ટાર્ટર.
words.usage_note: The starter course. (US spelling: 'appetizer'.)
examples: We shared an appetiser before the meal.
The soup was served as an appetiser.
Try the spring rolls as an appetiser.
Appetisers are listed at the top of the menu.

words.english_meaning: The largest or most important dish of a meal.
words.gujarati_meaning: ભોજનની મુખ્ય વાનગી.
words.usage_note: Comes after the appetiser and before dessert.
examples: For the main course, I had grilled fish.
The main course was served with rice.
We skipped the main course and went to dessert.
What will you have as a main course?

words.english_meaning: A drink, especially one other than water.
words.usage_note: A formal word for a drink; common on menus.
examples: Would you like a hot beverage?
The menu lists several cold beverages.
Tea is my favourite beverage.
Alcoholic beverages are not served here.

words.english_meaning: A note showing how much you must pay for a meal at a restaurant.
words.gujarati_meaning: ભોજનનું બિલ / હિસાબ.
words.usage_note: UK 'the bill', US 'the check'. 'Split the bill' = share the cost.
examples: Could we have the bill, please?
He kindly paid the bill.
Let's split the bill evenly.
The waiter brought the bill to our table.

words.english_meaning: A small extra amount of money given to someone for good service.
words.gujarati_meaning: સેવા બદલ અપાતી બક્ષિસ.
words.usage_note: Both noun and verb ('tip the waiter'). Extra money for good service.
examples: We left a generous tip for the waiter.
It's polite to tip for good service.
The service was poor, so we left no tip.
She tipped the driver a little extra.

words.english_meaning: An arrangement to have a table, room, or seat kept for you.
words.gujarati_meaning: ટેબલ/જગ્યા અગાઉથી બુક કરાવવી.
words.usage_note: 'Make/have a reservation' for a table or room.
examples: I made a reservation for two at eight.
Do you have a reservation, sir?
We had to cancel our dinner reservation.
It's wise to book a reservation on weekends.

words.english_meaning: Containing many of the substances the body needs to stay healthy.
words.gujarati_meaning: પોષણયુક્ત, શરીરને ફાયદાકારક.
words.usage_note: Food that is good for you. Noun: 'nutrition'.
examples: Vegetables are very nutritious.
She cooks nutritious meals for the family.
A nutritious breakfast keeps you energetic.
Fruits are a nutritious snack.

words.english_meaning: Good for your health; healthy and nourishing.
words.gujarati_meaning: તંદુરસ્ત, શરીર માટે સારું.
words.usage_note: Suggests simple, natural, healthy food.
examples: They serve wholesome, home-style food.
Oats make a wholesome breakfast.
We prefer wholesome ingredients.
A wholesome diet keeps you fit.

words.english_meaning: An amount of food served to or eaten by one person.
words.gujarati_meaning: એક વ્યક્તિ માટેનો ભોજનનો ભાગ / હિસ્સો.
words.usage_note: 'Portion size' = how much is served. Controlling portions helps health.
examples: The restaurant serves large portions.
Watch your portion sizes.
She gave me a small portion of rice.
Divide the cake into equal portions.

words.english_meaning: To have a very strong desire for a particular food.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ ખાવાની તીવ્ર ઇચ્છા થવી.
words.usage_note: 'Crave' + food; noun 'craving' = a strong urge.
examples: I'm craving something sweet.
She craves spicy food when stressed.
Pregnant women often crave odd foods.
After the gym, I crave a big meal.

words.english_meaning: To eat more food than you need or than is healthy.
words.gujarati_meaning: જરૂર કરતાં વધારે ખાવું.
words.usage_note: Eating too much; common at feasts/festivals.
examples: It's easy to overeat at a buffet.
I always overeat during festivals.
Try not to overeat before bed.
He overate and felt uncomfortable.

words.english_meaning: A way of eating that includes the right variety and amount of foods for health.
words.gujarati_meaning: પોષક તત્ત્વોથી ભરપૂર સંતુલિત આહાર.
words.usage_note: Includes carbs, protein, fats, and vitamins in proper proportion.
examples: A balanced diet keeps you healthy.
Doctors recommend a balanced diet.
She follows a balanced diet and exercises.
Children need a balanced diet to grow.

words.english_meaning: Extremely hungry.
words.gujarati_meaning: અતિશય ભૂખ્યું.
words.usage_note: A strong word for very hungry (stronger than 'hungry').
examples: I'm famished — let's eat now.
After the hike, we were all famished.
He looked famished and tired.
By lunchtime she was absolutely famished.

words.english_meaning: Slightly hungry.
words.usage_note: Informal British; mildly hungry — wanting a snack.
examples: I'm feeling a bit peckish.
If you're peckish, have some fruit.
We were peckish, so we shared a snack.
A peckish child kept asking for biscuits.

words.english_meaning: The natural desire to eat food.
words.gujarati_meaning: ભૂખ, ખાવાની ઇચ્છા.
words.usage_note: 'Lose your appetite' = not feel like eating.
examples: The walk gave me a good appetite.
He has a healthy appetite.
I lost my appetite when I felt ill.
The aroma whetted our appetite.

words.english_meaning: Having eaten enough; not able to eat any more.
words.gujarati_meaning: પેટ ભરાઈ ગયું હોવું.
words.usage_note: Informal for 'I've eaten enough'.
examples: No more for me, I'm full up.
We were full up after the feast.
I can't finish this — I'm full up.
The kids said they were full up.

words.english_meaning: To eat something by taking small bites.
words.gujarati_meaning: થોડું થોડું, ધીમે ધીમે ખાવું.
words.usage_note: Eating slowly in tiny bites; 'nibble on' a snack.
examples: She nibbled on a biscuit.
We nibbled at the snacks while chatting.
The mouse nibbled the cheese.
He nibbled his food without much appetite.

words.english_meaning: To eat something quickly and hungrily.
words.gujarati_meaning: ભૂખ્યાની જેમ ઝડપથી ખાઈ જવું.
words.usage_note: Eating fast and eagerly; the opposite of 'nibble'.
examples: The children devoured the pizza.
He devoured his dinner in minutes.
We were so hungry we devoured everything.
She devoured the cake hungrily.

words.english_meaning: A rare or special food that is considered especially nice to eat.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ ખાસ/દુર્લભ સ્વાદિષ્ટ વાનગી.
words.usage_note: A prized, often regional special food.
examples: This sweet is a local delicacy.
Fish curry is a delicacy in this region.
We tasted several delicacies on the trip.
Caviar is considered a delicacy.

words.english_meaning: A portion of food given to one person at a meal.
words.gujarati_meaning: એક વાર પીરસાતો ભોજનનો ભાગ.
words.usage_note: 'A second helping' = more of the same dish.
examples: Can I have a second helping, please?
She gave me a generous helping of rice.
He took a large helping of dessert.
There's enough for second helpings.

words.english_meaning: Made at home, not bought from a shop.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઘરે બનાવેલું.
words.usage_note: Implies fresh, personal cooking. (Also written 'home-made'.)
examples: I love homemade pickles.
The cake was homemade.
Homemade food is healthier.
She brought homemade cookies to share.

words.english_meaning: (Of food or drink) very hot.
words.gujarati_meaning: એકદમ ગરમાગરમ.
words.usage_note: An idiom for freshly cooked, very hot food.
examples: The soup was served piping hot.
Enjoy the rotis piping hot.
She brought out a piping hot pizza.
Nothing beats piping hot tea on a cold day.

words.english_meaning: To eat something quickly, often a small or casual meal.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઝડપથી થોડું ખાઈ લેવું.
words.usage_note: Informal — a quick, casual meal.
words.memory_tip: ઝડપથી થોડું ખાઈ લેવું = grab a bite.
examples: Let's grab a bite before the movie.
I only had time to grab a bite.
We grabbed a bite at a roadside stall.
Want to grab a bite after work?

words.english_meaning: To have a meal at a restaurant rather than at home.
words.gujarati_meaning: બહાર (રેસ્ટોરન્ટમાં) જમવું.
words.usage_note: The opposite of 'eat in' / 'cook at home'.
examples: Let's eat out tonight.
We eat out once a week.
They prefer eating out on weekends.
It's cheaper to cook than to eat out.

words.english_meaning: To start eating something eagerly and with enjoyment.
words.gujarati_meaning: ભૂખથી/ઉત્સાહથી ખાવાનું શરૂ કરવું.
words.usage_note: Informal British; 'tuck into' a meal = eat it heartily.
examples: The food's ready — tuck in!
They tucked into the feast happily.
He tucked into a big plate of biryani.
Don't wait for me; tuck in.

words.english_meaning: Having a sharp, pungent taste that is not sweet, like black coffee or dark chocolate.
words.gujarati_meaning: કડવો સ્વાદ — જેમ કે કાળી કૉફી અથવા ડાર્ક ચૉકલેટ જેવો તીખો, અળખામણો સ્વાદ.
words.usage_note: Used to describe a taste that many find unpleasant, though some foods like dark chocolate are valued for their bitterness.
words.memory_tip: 'bitter' = કડવું → bitter taste = કડવો સ્વાદ, જેવો કે કારેલાનો.
examples: The medicine had a bitter taste that was hard to swallow.
She prefers bitter dark chocolate over sweet milk chocolate.
The bitter flavour of the coffee woke him up instantly.
Bitter melon is commonly used in South Asian cooking.

words.english_meaning: Having an acidic taste like lemon juice or vinegar; not sweet.
words.gujarati_meaning: ખાટો સ્વાદ — જેવો કે લીંબુ અથવા વિનેગરનો, ન મીઠો.
words.usage_note: Sour is a basic taste descriptor. 'Turn sour' can also mean food has spoiled.
examples: The yogurt had a pleasantly sour taste.
She made a sour face after biting into the unripe mango.
Sour cream is used as a topping for baked potatoes.
The milk turned sour after being left out overnight.

words.english_meaning: Having the pleasant taste characteristic of sugar or honey.
words.gujarati_meaning: મીઠો સ્વાદ — ખાંડ અથવા મધ જેવો આહ્લાદક સ્વાદ.
words.usage_note: A 'sweet tooth' means a person who loves sweet foods. 'Bittersweet' describes something both good and sad.
examples: The ripe mango was incredibly sweet.
She has a sweet tooth and loves desserts.
The sauce had a sweet and sour balance.
This tea is too sweet for my taste.

words.english_meaning: Having a strong, hot flavour from spices such as chilli or pepper.
words.gujarati_meaning: મસાલેદાર અથવા તીખો — મરચા અથવા મરી જેવા મસાલાઓથી આવતો ઉગ્ર સ્વાદ.
words.usage_note: Spicy usually refers to heat from chilli. Do not confuse with 'spiced', which simply means seasoned with spices.
examples: He loves spicy food and always orders the hottest dish.
The curry was so spicy it made her eyes water.
Indian cuisine is known for its spicy flavours.
Add less chilli if you don't want it too spicy.

words.english_meaning: Having a flavour that resembles or is produced by smoke, often from grilling or barbecuing.
words.gujarati_meaning: ધૂમ્ +'ઓ જેવો સ્વાદ — ગ્રિલ અથવા બાર્બેક્યૂ કરવાથી આવતો ધ'ઓ-ભ'ર'ઓ સ'ડ'.
words.usage_note: Smoky paprika (smoked paprika) is a popular way to add smoky flavour without a grill. Smoky flavour is central to barbecue cuisine.
examples: The barbecued ribs had a wonderful smoky flavour.
She added smoked paprika for a smoky depth.
The cheese had a rich, smoky taste.
Smoky lentil soup is a winter favourite.

words.english_meaning: A savoury, meaty taste considered the fifth basic taste, found in foods like mushrooms, soy sauce, and aged cheese.
words.gujarati_meaning: પાંચમો મૂળ સ્વાદ — ઘૂંટાઈ ગયેલ, ભારે અને ભૂ' ,'ગ'ડ' એ'વ' સ'ડ', જ' ,'ઉ, ,'ઓ'ય ,'ઓ'સ, ,'ગ' ,'ઝ'.
words.usage_note: Umami is a Japanese word and concept, now widely used in English culinary contexts.
examples: Mushrooms add an umami depth to the soup.
Soy sauce is a great source of umami.
Chefs often use parmesan rind to add umami to sauces.
The umami flavour in the broth made it incredibly satisfying.

words.english_meaning: Having a sharply strong taste or smell that is often overpowering.
words.usage_note: Pungent describes both taste and smell. Often used for garlic, onions, or strong cheeses.
examples: The pungent smell of garlic filled the kitchen.
Blue cheese has a very pungent flavour.
Some people dislike the pungent taste of durian.
The pungent curry made everyone's eyes water.

words.english_meaning: Having a soft, smooth, and rich flavour without sharpness or bitterness.
words.usage_note: Mellow is often used for aged wines, cheeses, or coffees that have developed a smooth, rich character over time.
examples: The aged cheddar had a mellow, nutty flavour.
This wine is very mellow and easy to drink.
Roasting garlic makes it mellow and sweet.
The coffee had a mellow taste with hints of chocolate.

words.english_meaning: Having a sharp, acidic flavour; pleasantly sour.
words.usage_note: Tart implies a sharper, more refreshing sourness than simply 'sour'. Also a noun for a pastry with an open top.
examples: The cranberries were wonderfully tart.
She liked the tart flavour of the lemon tart.
Rhubarb has a naturally tart taste.
The dressing was tart but balanced with a little honey.

words.english_meaning: Lacking flavour or taste; dull and uninteresting to eat.
words.usage_note: Insipid is a formal, slightly literary word. In everyday speech, 'bland' or 'tasteless' are more common.
examples: The soup was watery and insipid.
She found the hospital food insipid and unappetising.
Without seasoning, the dish was completely insipid.
He complained that the boiled vegetables were insipid.

words.english_meaning: To briefly plunge food into boiling water and then into cold water to stop cooking, in order to soften or preserve colour.
words.usage_note: Blanching is a common prep technique before freezing vegetables to preserve their colour and texture.
examples: Blanch the broccoli for two minutes before adding it to the stir-fry.
She blanched the almonds to remove their skins easily.
Blanching spinach before freezing helps retain its bright green colour.
You should blanch the tomatoes before peeling them.

words.english_meaning: To cook food slowly in a small amount of liquid in a covered pot.
words.usage_note: Braising is ideal for tough cuts of meat as the slow cooking breaks down the fibres, making the meat tender.
examples: She braised the lamb shanks for three hours until tender.
Braising is the best method for tough cuts of beef.
He braised the cabbage with bacon and apple.
The slow-braised pork was falling off the bone.

words.english_meaning: To cut food into small, uniform cube-shaped pieces.
words.usage_note: Dicing is more precise than chopping — the pieces are uniform cubes. 'Finely diced' means very small cubes.
examples: Dice the onions before adding them to the pan.
She finely diced the carrots for the salad.
Diced tomatoes are used as a base for many sauces.
He diced the chicken into even pieces for the curry.

words.english_meaning: To gently mix a light ingredient into a heavier one using a soft cutting and turning motion to preserve air.
words.usage_note: Folding is used in baking to keep a mixture light and airy. Overmixing deflates the batter.
examples: Fold the egg whites gently into the batter.
She carefully folded the cream into the mousse.
Fold the flour in slowly to avoid lumps.
Over-folding the mixture will make the cake dense.

words.english_meaning: To cut food, especially meat or garlic, into very tiny pieces.
words.usage_note: Minced meat (or mince) is a common ingredient in dishes like bolognese or keema.
examples: Mince the garlic finely before adding it to the oil.
She used minced beef to make the bolognese sauce.
The recipe calls for a cup of minced onion.
He minced the herbs and mixed them into the butter.

words.english_meaning: To cook food gently in simmering liquid, such as water, milk, or stock.
words.usage_note: Poaching is a gentle, healthy cooking method that keeps food moist. Poached eggs are a brunch favourite.
examples: She poached the eggs perfectly for breakfast.
Poach the salmon in white wine for extra flavour.
Poaching is a healthy way to cook chicken.
He poached the pears in spiced red wine.

words.english_meaning: To boil a liquid so that it evaporates and becomes thicker and more concentrated in flavour.
words.usage_note: Reduction is a key technique in sauce-making. 'Reduce by half' means boil until only half the liquid remains.
examples: Reduce the sauce on a low heat until it thickens.
The recipe says to reduce the stock by half.
Reducing the wine before adding cream gives a rich flavour.
She reduced the balsamic vinegar into a glossy glaze.

words.english_meaning: To cook food by placing it over boiling water so that the steam cooks it without contact with the water.
words.usage_note: Steaming retains more nutrients than boiling. Dim sum dumplings are a famous example of steamed food.
examples: Steam the broccoli for five minutes to keep it crisp.
Steamed fish is healthier than fried fish.
She steamed the dumplings in a bamboo basket.
Steam the rice instead of boiling it for fluffier results.

words.english_meaning: To heat sugar or foods containing sugar until they turn golden-brown and develop a rich, sweet flavour.
words.usage_note: Caramelised onions take 30-45 minutes on low heat. The process requires patience to develop deep, sweet flavour.
examples: Caramelise the onions slowly for the best flavour.
He caramelised the sugar to make a toffee sauce.
Caramelised bananas are delicious over ice cream.
The caramelisation of the sugar gives creme brulee its crunchy top.

words.english_meaning: To melt fat from meat by cooking it slowly, so the fat runs out and the meat becomes crispy.
words.usage_note: Rendering is commonly used for bacon, duck, or pork belly. The rendered fat can be used for frying.
examples: Render the bacon in a cold pan for the crispiest result.
Slowly render the duck fat before roasting.
Rendered lard was traditionally used for pastry.
The pork skin becomes crispy as the fat renders out.

words.english_meaning: A meal cooked and bought at a restaurant but eaten somewhere else, or the shop that sells such food.
words.usage_note: British English uses 'takeaway'; American English uses 'takeout'. Both mean the same thing.
examples: Let's order a takeaway tonight instead of cooking.
They got a Chinese takeaway and watched a film.
Takeaway food has become very popular since food delivery apps launched.
She picked up a takeaway on her way home from work.

words.english_meaning: A list of food and drink items available at a restaurant.
words.usage_note: A 'set menu' is a fixed selection of dishes at a fixed price. An 'a la carte' menu allows ordering individual items.
examples: Could we see the menu, please?
The set menu includes three courses for a fixed price.
The children's menu has simpler options.
The seasonal menu changes every three months.

words.english_meaning: A person who serves food and drinks to customers in a restaurant.
words.usage_note: Waiter (male) and waitress (female) are traditional terms. 'Server' is now commonly used for any gender.
examples: The waiter took our order promptly.
Excuse me, waiter — could we have the bill?
The waiter recommended the chef's special.
She worked as a waitress during her university days.

words.english_meaning: Given free of charge, especially as a gesture of goodwill in a restaurant.
words.usage_note: 'On the house' and 'complimentary' are synonymous in restaurant contexts. Do not confuse with 'complementary' (goes well with).
examples: The restaurant offered complimentary bread while we waited.
We received a complimentary dessert on our anniversary.
The manager sent over a complimentary bottle of wine.
Complimentary tea is available in the lounge.

words.english_meaning: A charge made by a restaurant for serving wine that a customer has brought themselves.
words.usage_note: Some restaurants are 'BYO (bring your own)' restaurants where corkage applies. Always ask about the corkage fee in advance.
examples: The restaurant charges a corkage fee of 10 pounds per bottle.
We brought our own champagne and paid the corkage.
Ask if there is a corkage charge before bringing your own wine.
Some restaurants offer no corkage on certain nights.

words.english_meaning: To eat a main meal, especially in a formal or restaurant setting.
words.usage_note: 'Dine out' means to eat at a restaurant. 'Wine and dine' means to treat someone to a good meal and drinks.
examples: They dined at an Italian restaurant to celebrate.
We dine out at least once a week.
He wined and dined his clients at a luxury restaurant.
The hotel offers a dining experience with panoramic views.

words.english_meaning: The first course of a meal, served before the main dish.
words.usage_note: In British English, 'starter' is common; in American English, 'appetizer' or 'entree' is used for the first course.
examples: I'll have the soup as a starter, please.
The starter was a beautiful smoked salmon dish.
They shared a few starters before the main course.
The restaurant is known for its inventive starters.

words.english_meaning: A sweet course eaten at the end of a meal.
words.usage_note: In British English, 'pudding' or 'afters' are informal terms for dessert. Do not confuse 'dessert' (sweet dish) with 'desert' (dry land).
examples: Would you like to see the dessert menu?
She ordered a chocolate fondant for dessert.
He was too full for dessert after the large main course.
The desserts at this bakery are legendary.

words.english_meaning: One of the successive parts of a meal, such as starter, main, and dessert.
words.usage_note: A 'three-course meal' has a starter, main, and dessert. A 'tasting menu' may have seven or more courses.
examples: We had a three-course meal for our anniversary.
The first course was a delicate mushroom soup.
A five-course tasting menu is available on weekends.
They opted for the two-course lunch deal.

words.english_meaning: A bag provided by a restaurant to take home leftover food from a meal.
collocations: take home in a doggy bag
words.usage_note: The term originally referred to telling staff the food was for a pet. Now widely accepted in most countries.
examples: Could we have a doggy bag for the leftovers?
She took the rest of her pasta home in a doggy bag.
Asking for a doggy bag helps reduce food waste.
More restaurants now offer doggy bags as standard.

words.english_meaning: A unit of energy provided by food, used to measure the energy content of what we eat.
words.usage_note: Technically, food labels show 'kilocalories' (kcal), but these are commonly called 'calories' in everyday speech.
examples: An apple contains about 80 calories.
She tracks her calorie intake every day.
Exercise helps you burn calories.
A high-calorie diet can lead to weight gain.

words.english_meaning: A nutrient essential for building and repairing body tissues, found in meat, eggs, beans, and dairy.
words.usage_note: Protein is one of three macronutrients alongside carbohydrates and fats. Athletes often increase protein intake.
examples: Chicken breast is an excellent source of lean protein.
Vegetarians can get protein from lentils and tofu.
He increased his protein intake to build muscle.
Eggs are one of the most complete protein foods.

words.english_meaning: A substance in plant foods that the body cannot digest, which helps keep the digestive system healthy.
words.usage_note: Both spellings are correct: 'fibre' (British) and 'fiber' (American). A high-fibre diet is linked to a lower risk of bowel cancer.
examples: Wholemeal bread is high in dietary fibre.
A diet rich in fibre can reduce cholesterol.
Fruits and vegetables are excellent sources of fibre.
He increased his fibre intake to improve digestion.

words.english_meaning: A period of time during which a person avoids unhealthy food and drink to cleanse the body.
words.usage_note: The scientific evidence for 'detox diets' is limited. Nutritionists note the liver and kidneys naturally detoxify the body.
examples: She went on a detox after the holiday season.
He tried a week-long juice detox.
A detox diet typically involves avoiding alcohol, caffeine, and processed foods.
Many nutritionists are sceptical about commercial detox products.

words.english_meaning: Describing food that contains no gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye, suitable for people with coeliac disease.
words.usage_note: Coeliac disease requires a strict gluten-free diet. Many people also choose gluten-free diets by preference, though this is not medically necessary.
examples: She follows a gluten-free diet due to coeliac disease.
The restaurant has a separate gluten-free menu.
Many supermarkets now stock a wide range of gluten-free products.
Gluten-free pasta is made from rice or maize flour.

words.english_meaning: A person who does not eat or use any animal products, including meat, dairy, and eggs.
words.usage_note: Veganism extends beyond diet to exclude animal products in clothing and cosmetics. Do not confuse with vegetarian, who may eat dairy and eggs.
examples: She became a vegan for environmental reasons.
Most restaurants now offer vegan options.
A vegan diet excludes all animal products.
He switched to a vegan lifestyle last year.

words.english_meaning: The chemical processes in the body that convert food into energy.
words.usage_note: A 'fast metabolism' means the body burns calories quickly. Exercise and certain foods are said to boost metabolism.
examples: Exercise can help boost your metabolism.
Her fast metabolism means she can eat a lot without gaining weight.
Thyroid problems can slow down your metabolism.
Green tea is believed to slightly increase metabolic rate.

words.english_meaning: A negative physical reaction to a particular food, such as difficulty digesting it, without an immune response.
words.usage_note: Food intolerance differs from a food allergy. Allergy involves the immune system; intolerance usually involves digestion.
examples: She has lactose intolerance and avoids dairy.
A food intolerance test can identify problem foods.
Lactose intolerance is very common in South Asian populations.
He discovered his intolerance to gluten after years of stomach problems.

words.english_meaning: A product taken to add vitamins, minerals, or other nutrients to the diet that may be missing.
words.usage_note: A supplement should complement, not replace, a healthy diet. Always consult a doctor before starting supplements.
examples: She takes a vitamin D supplement in winter.
Protein supplements are popular among gym-goers.
A balanced diet reduces the need for dietary supplements.
He supplements his diet with omega-3 fish oil capsules.

words.english_meaning: The process of maintaining adequate water levels in the body, essential for health.
words.usage_note: The body loses water through sweat, breathing, and urination. Adults are advised to drink about 2 litres of water a day.
examples: Proper hydration is essential during exercise.
He was suffering from dehydration after running the marathon.
Fruits and vegetables also contribute to daily hydration.
She carries a water bottle everywhere to stay hydrated.

words.english_meaning: Extremely hungry; feeling an intense desire to eat.
words.usage_note: Ravenous is stronger than 'hungry' or 'peckish'. It suggests an almost desperate need to eat.
examples: I am absolutely ravenous — I haven't eaten since breakfast.
The children came home from school ravenous.
After the hike, they were ravenous and ate everything in sight.
She had a ravenous appetite after being unwell for a week.

words.english_meaning: Completely satisfied after eating, with no desire to eat more.
words.usage_note: Satiated implies deep satisfaction beyond simply being 'full'. It is more formal than 'full up'.
examples: After the three-course meal, she was completely satiated.
High-protein foods keep you satiated for longer.
He felt satiated and content after the feast.
Fibre-rich foods help you feel satiated and prevent overeating.

words.english_meaning: To eat small amounts of food throughout the day rather than having set meals.
words.usage_note: Grazing can be a healthy eating pattern for some but may lead to overeating if snacks are high in calories.
examples: She tends to graze on snacks all day rather than eat proper meals.
Grazing on fruit and nuts is a healthy habit.
He grazed on leftovers while watching television.
Some nutritionists recommend grazing over three big meals.

words.english_meaning: Sharp, uncomfortable feelings of pain in the stomach caused by hunger.
words.usage_note: Hunger pangs occur when the stomach contracts in search of food. They typically last about 30 minutes.
examples: She felt hunger pangs by mid-morning as she had skipped breakfast.
Drink water to temporarily ease hunger pangs.
He ignored his hunger pangs and worked through lunch.
Hunger pangs woke him up in the middle of the night.

words.english_meaning: To eat a large amount of food greedily and to excess.
words.usage_note: Gorge implies eating well beyond what is needed. Often used reflexively: 'gorge oneself on something'.
examples: They gorged themselves on pizza after the football match.
She gorged on sweets during the festival.
It's tempting to gorge on buffet food, but try to pace yourself.
He gorged on holiday food and felt unwell afterwards.

words.english_meaning: To stimulate someone's appetite or desire for food.
words.usage_note: Used almost exclusively in the phrase 'whet the appetite'. Do not confuse with 'wet'.
examples: The smell of freshly baked bread whetted her appetite.
The teaser video whetted viewers' appetites for the new show.
A starter is meant to whet your appetite, not fill you up.
The aroma of spices whetted his appetite as he walked past the restaurant.

words.english_meaning: A small amount of food eaten between main meals.
words.usage_note: Snacking between meals can help maintain energy levels. Healthy snacks include fruit, nuts, and yoghurt.
examples: She keeps healthy snacks at her desk to avoid vending machine food.
He snacked on almonds between meetings.
Children often need an afternoon snack after school.
Late-night snacking can disrupt sleep and digestion.

words.english_meaning: To allow oneself to enjoy something pleasurable, especially food, beyond what is usual or advisable.
words.usage_note: Indulge implies pleasure with a slight sense of guilt or going beyond normal limits. 'Occasional indulgence' is a common phrase.
examples: She indulged in a large slice of chocolate cake.
It's fine to indulge occasionally as part of a balanced diet.
He indulged his sweet tooth with a box of chocolates.
Everyone deserves to indulge in their favourite food sometimes.

words.english_meaning: To deliberately choose not to eat or drink something, often for health or moral reasons.
words.usage_note: Abstain often implies willpower and self-discipline. 'Abstinence' refers to the state of abstaining.
examples: She abstained from alcohol during her pregnancy.
He abstained from meat during the religious festival.
Abstaining from sugar for a month helped him lose weight.
Many people abstain from eating after 8 pm to improve digestion.

words.english_meaning: To eat a very large amount of food in a short time, usually beyond what is comfortable.
words.usage_note: Binge eating can be a sign of an eating disorder. 'Binge-eating disorder' is a recognised medical condition requiring professional support.
examples: She binged on crisps and chocolate while watching films.
Binge eating followed by guilt is a warning sign.
He tends to binge at weekends after being strict all week.
Binge eating disorder affects millions of people worldwide.

words.english_meaning: Splendid and expensive-looking; describing a meal that is rich, lavish, and impressive.
words.usage_note: Sumptuous emphasises luxury and abundance. Often used for formal dinners or special occasions.
examples: The wedding feast was absolutely sumptuous.
They enjoyed a sumptuous three-course dinner at the hotel.
The table was laid with a sumptuous spread of dishes.
A sumptuous banquet was held in honour of the visiting dignitaries.

words.english_meaning: Stimulating one's appetite; looking or smelling attractive and making you want to eat.
words.usage_note: Appetising can describe appearance and smell. Its antonym, 'unappetising', is equally useful.
examples: The golden-brown chicken looked incredibly appetising.
The appetising aroma of garlic butter filled the room.
Colourful dishes always look more appetising.
She arranged the fruit to make the platter look appetising.

words.english_meaning: Lacking strong flavour, taste, or interest; mild and unexciting.
words.usage_note: Bland is not always negative — bland foods (rice, toast, banana) are recommended when someone is unwell.
examples: Hospital food is often criticised for being bland.
The soup was bland and needed more seasoning.
A bland diet is recommended after a stomach illness.
She found the salad bland without any dressing.

words.english_meaning: Good for health and well-being; describing food that is healthy, natural, and nourishing.
words.usage_note: Wholesome implies both physical and moral goodness — it often carries a warm, comforting connotation.
examples: She prepared a wholesome meal of grilled fish and vegetables.
The children enjoyed wholesome homemade soup.
Wholesome ingredients make for better cooking.
A wholesome breakfast sets you up for the day.

words.english_meaning: Rich, satisfying, and rather excessive — describing food that is pleasurable and possibly unhealthy.
words.usage_note: Indulgent has a positive, pleasurable connotation even though it implies something a little excessive or unhealthy.
examples: The chocolate lava cake was wonderfully indulgent.
She treated herself to an indulgent spa lunch.
It's fine to enjoy an indulgent meal occasionally.
He ordered the most indulgent item on the menu — triple chocolate brownie.

words.english_meaning: Extremely tasty and delicious; informally used to describe food that is wonderful to eat.
words.usage_note: Scrumptious is informal and enthusiastic. It is typically used in spoken English to express great pleasure at food.
examples: The homemade pie was absolutely scrumptious.
Everything at that bakery is scrumptious.
She made a scrumptious lasagne for the dinner party.
This is the most scrumptious chocolate cake I have ever tasted.

words.english_meaning: Having a pleasant and distinctive flavour; full of taste.
words.usage_note: Both 'flavoursome' (British) and 'flavorful' (American) mean the same thing. 'Flavoursome' is less common but found in British recipe writing.
examples: The slow-cooked lamb was incredibly flavoursome.
Fresh herbs make any dish more flavoursome.
The sauce was rich and flavoursome.
She used high-quality ingredients to create a flavoursome meal.

words.english_meaning: Cooked for too long, making the food dry, tough, or less flavourful.
words.usage_note: Overcooked meat becomes dry and tough; overcooked vegetables lose their nutrients and colour.
examples: The steak was unfortunately overcooked and quite tough.
Overcooked pasta loses its texture and becomes mushy.
She returned the overcooked chicken to the kitchen.
Overcooked vegetables lose most of their vitamins.

words.english_meaning: Not cooked enough; still raw in the centre or lacking enough heat to be safe or pleasant to eat.
words.usage_note: Undercooked poultry and eggs can pose serious food safety risks due to bacteria like Salmonella.
examples: The chicken was undercooked in the middle — dangerous to eat.
She sent back the undercooked rice.
Undercooked eggs can carry a risk of Salmonella.
The restaurant apologised for serving undercooked fish.

words.english_meaning: Decorated or embellished with a small amount of food, such as herbs, lemon, or sauce, to enhance its appearance.
words.usage_note: A garnish should complement the dish's flavour, not just its appearance. Common garnishes include parsley, lemon wedges, and chilli flakes.
examples: The soup was garnished with a swirl of cream and fresh chives.
Each plate was beautifully garnished with a slice of lemon.
She garnished the curry with fresh coriander leaves.
A well-garnished dish signals care and attention from the chef.

mini_dialogues.title: Deciding to eat out
mini_dialogues.situation: Two friends plan dinner.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'm famished. Shall we eat out tonight?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Sure! I've been craving some good Italian cuisine.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Let me make a reservation for two.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Great — I could really tuck into a big bowl of pasta.

mini_dialogues.title: At the restaurant
mini_dialogues.situation: Ordering a meal with a waiter.

turns.speaker: Waiter
turns.text: What will you have as a main course?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: The grilled fish, please, and a cold beverage.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Shall we order an appetiser to share?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes — and let's remember to leave a tip.

mini_dialogues.title: Cooking at home
mini_dialogues.situation: You praise a friend's home cooking.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: This homemade curry smells mouth-watering!

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Thanks. I let it simmer and seasoned it well.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Did you garnish it with coriander?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Of course. Tuck in while it's piping hot!

mini_dialogues.title: Eating healthily
mini_dialogues.situation: Talking about diet.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'm trying to follow a balanced diet.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Good idea — eat more nutritious, wholesome food.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: But I still crave sweets sometimes.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: A small portion now and then is fine.

mini_dialogues.title: A snack break
mini_dialogues.situation: Offering a snack before dinner.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Are you hungry?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Just a little peckish, actually.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: There are some biscuits — nibble on those for now.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Thanks. I don't want to overeat before dinner.

quiz.instructions: Choose the correct option. Questions test meaning (English<->Gujarati), fill-in-the-blank, synonyms, antonyms, and definitions.

questions.question: What is the Gujarati meaning of 'Bland'?

An 'appetiser' is best described as:
options: A small dish served before the main course
The main dish of a meal
A sweet eaten at the end
questions.answer: A small dish served before the main course

questions.question: Which word can replace 'Mouth-watering'?

Could we have the ____, please? (after the meal)

Let's ____ tonight instead of cooking.

I made a ____ for two at eight o'clock.

words.english_meaning: To share or exchange information, ideas, or feelings with others.
words.gujarati_meaning: માહિતી, વિચારો અથવા ભાવનાઓ બીજા સાથે શેર કરવી અથવા આપ-લે કરવી.
words.usage_note: Used in professional contexts to stress clarity and effectiveness of information exchange.
examples: She communicates very clearly with her team.
He failed to communicate the deadline properly.
We need to communicate the changes to all departments.
It is important to communicate professionally via email.

words.english_meaning: Written communication, especially letters or emails exchanged between people or organizations.
words.gujarati_meaning: પત્ર અથવા ઈ-મેઇલ દ્વારા થતો સત્તાવાર સંવાદ.
words.usage_note: Often refers to formal written exchange in business or legal settings.
words.memory_tip: 'correspond' = co + respond → સાથે જવાબ આપવો → correspondence = letter exchange.
examples: All official correspondence must be filed.
She handles the correspondence with overseas clients.
The lawyer reviewed the correspondence before the trial.
Business correspondence should always be polite and professional.

words.english_meaning: A short official written message sent within an organization.
words.gujarati_meaning: સંસ્થામાં આંતરિક રીતે મોકલવામાં આવતો ટૂંકો સત્તાવાર સંદેશ.
words.usage_note: Short for 'memorandum'; commonly used in offices for quick internal announcements.
words.memory_tip: 'memo' = memory + note → યાદ અપાવવા માટેની ચિઠ્ઠી.
examples: The manager sent a memo about the new policy.
Please circulate this memo to all staff.
I received a memo regarding tomorrow's meeting.
Write a memo to the HR department about the holiday schedule.

words.english_meaning: A formal plan or suggestion put forward for consideration.
words.gujarati_meaning: વિચારણા માટે રજૂ કરવામાં આવેલ ઔપચારિક યોજના અથવા સૂચન.
words.usage_note: A 'proposal' is more formal than a suggestion and usually includes supporting details.
words.memory_tip: 'proposal' = pro + pose → 'આગળ' + 'મૂકવું' → proposal = આગળ મૂકવામાં આવેલ વિચાર.
examples: She submitted a proposal for the new project.
The board approved the business proposal.
His proposal was rejected due to budget constraints.
We need a detailed proposal before moving forward.

words.english_meaning: A meeting where information or instructions are given to a group.
words.gujarati_meaning: જૂથને માહિતી અથવા સૂચનાઓ આપવામાં આવે તેવી બેઠક.
words.usage_note: Often used in military, government, or corporate settings before an event or action.
examples: The team had a briefing before the client visit.
The manager conducted a morning briefing.
She gave a briefing on the new safety procedures.
Attend the media briefing at 10 AM.

words.english_meaning: Information given to someone about their performance or work to help them improve.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ વ્યક્તિને તેના કામ અથવા પ્રદર્શન વિશે આપવામાં આવેલ સૂચન અથવા અભિપ્રાય.
words.usage_note: 'Constructive feedback' is positive and helpful; 'negative feedback' points out faults.
words.memory_tip: 'feed' + 'back' → પાછું ખવડાવવું → feedback = response back to improve.
examples: The manager gave positive feedback on the report.
Please share your feedback after the session.
Constructive feedback helps employees grow.
She was nervous about receiving feedback on her presentation.

words.english_meaning: A list of topics or items to be discussed or acted upon.
words.gujarati_meaning: ચર્ચા અથવા કાર્ય માટેની બાબતોની યાદી.
words.usage_note: Also used figuratively: 'What's your agenda?' means what are your hidden motives.
words.memory_tip: 'agenda' = 'a genda' → Latin: 'things to be done' → કરવાની વાતોની યાદી.
examples: The agenda for today's meeting includes budget review.
She set the agenda before the conference.
There was no hidden agenda in his proposal.
The chairman distributed the agenda in advance.

words.english_meaning: To discuss something in order to reach an agreement.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ બાબત પર સહમત થવા માટે ચર્ચા કરવી.
words.usage_note: Negotiation requires compromise from both sides.
words.memory_tip: 'negotiate' = ne + go + tiate → 'ના' + 'જાઓ' → ના-ના કરીને agreement → negotiate.
examples: They negotiated the contract terms for three hours.
She is skilled at negotiating salary packages.
Both companies agreed to negotiate a new deal.
The union and management negotiated a fair wage increase.

words.english_meaning: A formal talk or display of information to an audience.
words.gujarati_meaning: પ્રેક્ષકો સમક્ષ માહિતી રજૂ કરવાની ઔપચારિક રીત.
words.usage_note: Can be oral, visual, or both; often includes slides in a corporate setting.
examples: He gave an impressive presentation on market trends.
She prepared slides for her presentation.
The presentation lasted forty-five minutes.
Our team's presentation won the client's approval.

words.english_meaning: A formal document that presents findings, information, or analysis.
words.gujarati_meaning: તારણો, માહિતી અથવા વિશ્લેષણ રજૂ કરતો ઔપચારિક દસ્તાવેજ.
words.usage_note: Reports can be written or verbal; written reports are more common in offices.
words.memory_tip: 'report' = re + port → 'ફરી' + 'લઈ જવું' → report = information carried back.
examples: The quarterly report was submitted on time.
She wrote a detailed report on the incident.
He reported the findings to the board.
The annual report showed strong financial growth.

words.english_meaning: The latest time or date by which something must be completed.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ કામ પૂર્ણ કરવા માટેની છેલ્લી તારીખ અથવા સમય.
words.usage_note: Missing a deadline in professional settings can have serious consequences.
words.memory_tip: 'deadline' = dead + line → 'dead' = ખતમ → deadline = ખતમ થવાની line = છેલ્લો સમય.
examples: We must meet the project deadline by Friday.
She always delivers her work before the deadline.
The team missed the deadline due to technical issues.
Set realistic deadlines to avoid burnout.

words.english_meaning: To make something clearer and easier to understand.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ બાબત વધુ સ્પષ્ટ અને સમજવા સરળ બનાવવી.
words.usage_note: Often used to politely request more information: 'Can you clarify that?'
words.memory_tip: 'clarify' = clarity + fy → clarity = સ્પષ્ટતા → clarify = સ્પષ્ટ કરવું.
examples: Can you clarify what you mean by that?
She clarified the instructions for the new staff.
Please clarify your role in the project.
He asked for a moment to clarify his thoughts.

words.english_meaning: To give a brief statement of the main points of something.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ બાબતના મુખ્ય મુદ્દા ટૂંકમાં રજૂ કરવા.
words.usage_note: Often used at the end of meetings or reports to review main points.
words.memory_tip: 'summarize' = summary + ize → summary = સારાંશ → summarize = સારાંશ આપવો.
examples: Can you summarize the main points of the meeting?
She summarized the report in three bullet points.
He summarized the client's concerns for the team.
Please summarize the discussion in the minutes.

words.english_meaning: A formal request for information or an investigation into something.
words.gujarati_meaning: માહિતી માટે ઔપચારિક વિનંતી અથવા કોઈ બાબત અંગેની તપાસ.
words.usage_note: In British English often spelled 'enquiry'; 'inquiry' is more common in American English.
examples: She made an inquiry about the job opening.
All customer inquiries must be answered within 24 hours.
The company launched a formal inquiry into the incident.
He sent an email inquiry to the supplier.

words.english_meaning: To confirm receipt of something or recognize someone's contribution.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ વસ્તુ મળ્યાની પુષ્ટિ કરવી અથવા કોઈ વ્યક્તિના યોગદાનને સ્વીકારવું.
words.usage_note: In emails: 'I acknowledge receipt of your message' confirms you received it.
words.memory_tip: 'acknowledge' = ac + know + ledge → 'know' = જાણવું → acknowledge = જાણ્યાનો સ્વીકાર.
examples: Please acknowledge receipt of this email.
The manager acknowledged the team's hard work.
She acknowledged the mistake and corrected it.
He acknowledged the client's concerns during the meeting.

words.english_meaning: The act of assigning responsibility or authority to another person.
words.gujarati_meaning: બીજ વ્યક્તિને જવાબદારી અથવা અધિકાર સોંપવાની ક્રિયા.
words.usage_note: Good managers use delegation to empower their teams and manage time effectively.
words.memory_tip: 'delegate' = de + legate → legate = 'ambassador' → delegation = sending someone else to act.
examples: Effective delegation improves team productivity.
She used delegation to manage her heavy workload.
The CEO relied on delegation to run the company.
Poor delegation leads to confusion in responsibilities.

words.english_meaning: Intended to be kept secret and not shared with others.
words.gujarati_meaning: ગુપ્ત રાખવા માટે અભિપ્રેત; જે અન્ય સાથે શેર ન કરવી.
words.usage_note: Documents marked 'confidential' should not be shared outside the organization.
words.memory_tip: 'confidential' = confidence + ial → confidence = વિશ્વાસ → confidential = વિશ્વાસઘાત ન કરો.
examples: The report is strictly confidential.
All employee records are kept confidential.
Do not share confidential information with third parties.
She signed a confidential agreement before starting the project.

words.english_meaning: A small, enclosed workspace within a larger open office area.
words.gujarati_meaning: મોટા ઓફિસ વિસ્તારની અંદર નાની, અર્ધ-ઘેરાયેલ કામ કરવાની જગ્યા.
words.usage_note: Common in large corporate offices; gives semi-privacy in an open layout.
words.memory_tip: 'cubicle' = cube + icle → cube = ઘન → cubicle = cube જેવી નાની જગ્યા.
examples: She decorated her cubicle with family photos.
He worked in a cubicle on the third floor.
The open office replaced cubicles with shared desks.
A cubicle provides some privacy in a large office.

words.english_meaning: A desk or area equipped with a computer and accessories for one person to work.
words.gujarati_meaning: એક વ્યક્તિ માટે કમ્પ્યૂટર અને સાધનો સાથે સજ્જ ડેસ્ક અથવા કાર્ય-વિસ્તાર.
words.usage_note: In IT, a workstation can also refer to a powerful desktop computer.
words.memory_tip: 'workstation' = work + station → work = કામ + station = સ્ટૉપ → workstation = કામ કરવાની જગ્યા.
examples: Each employee has their own workstation.
He set up a new workstation for the intern.
The workstation was equipped with dual monitors.
An ergonomic workstation reduces back pain.

words.english_meaning: The area at the entrance of an office where visitors are greeted.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઑફિસના પ્રવેશ પર આવેલ વિસ્તાર જ્યાં મુલાકાતીઓનું સ્વાગત થાય છે.
words.usage_note: A 'receptionist' works at the reception and manages visitors and calls.
words.memory_tip: 'reception' = receive + tion → receive = સ્વીકારવું → reception = સ્વાગત-ક્ષેત્ર.
examples: Please wait at the reception until someone comes.
The receptionist greeted all visitors warmly.
All guests must sign in at the reception desk.
The reception area was redesigned to look more professional.

words.english_meaning: A room in an office used for meetings and group discussions.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઑફિસમાં બેઠકો અને ગ્રૂપ ચર્ચા માટે ઉપયોગમાં લેવાતો ઓરડો.
words.usage_note: Usually equipped with a large table, chairs, projector, and whiteboard.
words.memory_tip: 'conference' = together + talk → conference room = સૌ સાથે મળીને વાત કરે ત્યાં.
examples: Book the conference room for the 3 PM meeting.
The conference room seats up to twenty people.
She presented her findings in the conference room.
The conference room is equipped with video call facilities.

words.english_meaning: Writing and office materials such as pens, paper, and envelopes.
words.gujarati_meaning: કલમ, કાગળ, કવર જેવી લેખન અને ઑફિસ સામગ્રી.
words.usage_note: Do not confuse with 'stationary' (not moving); stationery = office supplies.
words.memory_tip: 'stationery' → remember 'e' for 'envelope' → stationery = envelope + writing things.
examples: The office stationery was ordered last week.
She picked up stationery from the supply room.
We need to restock the stationery cabinet.
Branded stationery gives a professional impression.

words.english_meaning: A machine that produces printed copies of digital documents.
words.gujarati_meaning: ડિજિટલ દસ્તાવેજોની છાપેલ નકલ બનાવતું ઉપકરણ.
words.usage_note: Common office issue: 'printer jam' means paper is stuck inside the printer.
words.memory_tip: 'printer' = print + er → print = છાપવું → printer = છાપનાર મશીન.
examples: The printer ran out of ink during the presentation.
Please print the report on the office printer.
The printer is on the second floor near the kitchen.
He fixed the printer jam before the meeting.

words.english_meaning: A white surface used for writing with markers during meetings or training.
words.gujarati_meaning: બેઠક અથવા તાલીમ દરમિયાન માર્કરથી લખવા માટે ઉપયોગમાં લેવાતી સફેદ સપાટી.
words.usage_note: Used widely in brainstorming sessions and training rooms.
words.memory_tip: 'whiteboard' = white + board → સફેદ + ફળિયું → whiteboard = white writing board.
examples: She drew the process diagram on the whiteboard.
The trainer used the whiteboard to explain concepts.
Erase the whiteboard before the next meeting.
An interactive whiteboard is connected to the computer.

words.english_meaning: A device that projects images or slides onto a screen.
words.gujarati_meaning: સ્ક્રીન પર ચિત્રો અથવા સ્લાઇડ્સ દર્શાવતું ઉપકરણ.
words.usage_note: Common in boardrooms and classrooms for displaying presentations.
words.memory_tip: 'projector' = project + or → project = ફેંકવું → projector = image ફેંકે.
examples: Connect the laptop to the projector before the meeting.
The projector bulb needs to be replaced.
She used the projector to display the sales charts.
Make sure the projector is working before the presentation.

words.english_meaning: A small room or area in an office where food, drinks, and kitchen supplies are kept.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઑફિસમાં ખોરાક, પીણાં અને રસોઈ-સામગ્રી રાખવા માટેનો નાનો ઓરડો.
words.usage_note: Often a social space where colleagues gather during breaks.
words.memory_tip: 'pantry' = pan + try → pan = વાસણ → pantry = pan and food store.
examples: She had her coffee break in the office pantry.
The pantry was stocked with snacks and beverages.
Please keep the pantry clean after use.
They held a quick discussion in the pantry.

words.english_meaning: A piece of furniture with drawers for storing files and documents.
words.gujarati_meaning: ફાઇલો અને દસ્તાવેજો સંગ્રહ કરવા માટે ખાના ધરાવતો ફર્નિચરનો ટુકડો.
words.usage_note: Important documents are often kept in locked filing cabinets for security.
words.memory_tip: 'filing' = file + ing → file = ફાઇલ → filing cabinet = ફાઇલ સ્ટોર.
examples: The contract is in the filing cabinet.
She organized all documents into the filing cabinet.
Lock the filing cabinet before leaving the office.
The filing cabinet is overflowing with old records.

words.english_meaning: Designed for comfort and efficiency in the working environment.
words.gujarati_meaning: કામ કરવાના વાતાવરણમાં આરામ અને કાર્યક્ષમતા માટે ડિઝાઇન કરેલ.
words.usage_note: Ergonomic design helps prevent repetitive strain injuries and back pain.
words.memory_tip: 'ergonomic' = ergo (work) + nomic (law) → worklaw → work comfort design.
examples: She invested in an ergonomic chair to avoid back pain.
The company provided ergonomic keyboards to all staff.
An ergonomic setup increases productivity.
Ergonomic furniture is essential in modern offices.

words.english_meaning: A board on a wall where notices and announcements are posted.
words.gujarati_meaning: દિવાલ પર લગાડેલ બૉર્ડ જ્યાં નોટિસ અને જાહેરાતો લગાડવામાં આવે છે.
words.usage_note: Used in offices, schools, and communities to share general information.
words.memory_tip: 'bulletin' = bullet + in → bulletin board = notices 'fired' at the public.
examples: She pinned the schedule to the bulletin board.
Check the bulletin board for the latest announcements.
The event notice was posted on the bulletin board.
They used the bulletin board to share motivational quotes.

words.english_meaning: Describing an office layout with few or no walls, encouraging collaboration.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઑફિસ ડિઝાઇન જ્યાં ઓછી અથવા ન જ ઓ walls હોય, teamwork ને પ્રોત્સાહ આપે.
words.usage_note: Open-plan offices encourage collaboration but can reduce individual privacy.
words.memory_tip: 'open-plan' = open + plan → ખુલ્લી + ગોઠવણ → open-plan = ખુલ્લી ઑફિસ.
examples: The company moved to an open-plan office to boost teamwork.
Many employees prefer private offices over open-plan layouts.
The open-plan design allows easy communication.
An open-plan office reduces noise barriers.

words.english_meaning: A system where employees use any available desk rather than having a fixed one.
words.gujarati_meaning: એ પ્રણાલી જ્યાં કર્મચારીઓ ગમે ત્યારે ઉપલબ્ધ ડેસ્ક ઉપયોગ કરે, નિશ્ચિત ડેસ્ક ન હોય.
words.usage_note: Common in companies with hybrid work models where not everyone is in the office every day.
words.memory_tip: 'hot-desking' = hot + desk → 'hot' = popular/in demand → grab any available desk.
examples: The company introduced hot-desking to save space.
Hot-desking requires employees to clear their desk daily.
She didn't enjoy hot-desking as she missed her own space.
Hot-desking is common in companies with remote-first policies.

words.english_meaning: A private internal network used within an organization for sharing information.
words.gujarati_meaning: સંસ્થામાં આંતરિક રીતે માહિતી શેર કરવા માટે ઉપયોગમાં લેવાતું ખાનગી નેટવર્ક.
words.usage_note: Unlike the internet, the intranet is accessible only to employees of the organization.
words.memory_tip: 'intranet' = intra (inside) + net → inside network → ઑફિસ અંદરનું internet.
examples: All policies are available on the company intranet.
Log in to the intranet to access HR forms.
The intranet was updated with the new office guidelines.
She posted the newsletter on the intranet.

words.english_meaning: A room in an office where stationery and other supplies are stored.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઑફિસ સ્ટેશનરી અને અન્ય સામગ્રી સ્ટોર કરવા માટેનો ઓરડો.
words.usage_note: Employees usually sign out items taken from the supply room to manage inventory.
words.memory_tip: 'supply room' = supply + room → supply = સામગ્રી → supply room = સામગ્રી ઓરડો.
examples: Get extra pens from the supply room.
The supply room is locked after 6 PM.
She restocked the supply room with printer paper.
All office supplies are kept in the supply room.

words.english_meaning: An ID card worn by employees to identify themselves and access office areas.
words.gujarati_meaning: કર્મચારીઓ દ્વારા ઓળખ અને ઑફિસ વિસ્તારોમાં પ્રવેશ માટે પહેરવામાં આવતું ID કાર્ડ.
words.usage_note: In secure offices, employees swipe their badge to enter restricted areas.
words.memory_tip: 'badge' = ઓળખ-ચિહ્ન → badge = your identity at work.
examples: Always wear your badge while in the office.
She forgot her badge and couldn't enter the building.
Swipe your badge at the entrance gate.
The security guard checked everyone's badge.

words.english_meaning: The official written record of what was discussed and decided in a meeting.
words.gujarati_meaning: બેઠકમાં શું ચર્ચ્યું અને શું નક્કી થ્યું તેનો સત્તાવાર લેખિત રેકૉર્ડ.
words.usage_note: Minutes are usually written by a secretary or designated note-taker.
words.memory_tip: 'minutes' = minute + s → small notes → meeting ની ટૂંકી નોંધ.
examples: She was asked to take the minutes at the board meeting.
The minutes were circulated to all attendees.
Please refer to last week's minutes for the decision.
The minutes were approved at the start of the meeting.

words.english_meaning: The minimum number of members required to be present to make a meeting valid.
words.gujarati_meaning: બેઠકને માન્ય ઠરાવવા માટે ઉપસ્થિત હોવા જ જોઈએ તેવા ન્યૂ nतम સભ્યોની સંખ્યા.
words.usage_note: If a quorum is not reached, the meeting cannot officially proceed.
words.memory_tip: 'quorum' = Latin 'of whom' → quorum = 'of whom enough must be present'.
examples: The meeting was postponed because there was no quorum.
A quorum of ten members is required for voting.
We need to confirm the quorum before starting.
The chairperson declared that the quorum was met.

words.english_meaning: The person who leads or presides over a meeting.
words.gujarati_meaning: બેઠકની અધ્યક્ષતા કરનાર વ્યક્તિ.
words.usage_note: Gender-neutral term replacing 'chairman'; 'chair' is also widely used.
words.memory_tip: 'chairperson' = chair + person → chair = ખુરશી → chairperson = ખુરશી વળો = leader.
examples: The chairperson opened the meeting at 9 AM.
She was elected chairperson of the committee.
The chairperson called for a vote on the proposal.
The chairperson ensured all voices were heard.

words.english_meaning: Tasks or decisions assigned to individuals at the end of a meeting.
words.gujarati_meaning: બેઠકના અંતે વ્યક્તિઓને સોંપવામાં આવેલ કાર્ય અથવા નિર્ણય.
words.usage_note: Action points ensure accountability; each item should have an owner and a deadline.
words.memory_tip: 'action points' = action + points → action = ક્રિયા → action points = કામ કરવાની યાદી.
examples: The meeting ended with a list of action points.
She followed up on all action points from last week.
Each action point was assigned to a team member.
Review the action points before the next meeting.

words.english_meaning: To generate many ideas spontaneously in a group discussion.
words.gujarati_meaning: ગ્રૂપ ચર્ચામાં સ્વ-ચ-સ્ફૂર્ત ઘણા વિચારો ઉત્પન્ન કરવા.
words.usage_note: In brainstorming, no idea is rejected initially; all suggestions are welcome.
words.memory_tip: 'brainstorm' = brain + storm → brain = મગજ + storm = તોફान → ideas ની વંટોળ.
examples: Let's brainstorm ideas for the new marketing campaign.
The team held a brainstorming session on Friday.
They brainstormed solutions to the customer complaint.
Brainstorming helps uncover creative approaches.

words.english_meaning: To make a process or meeting easier to run or manage.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ પ્રક્રિયા અથવા બેઠક સરળ અને સ્ઝ્ = manage કરવા-લાયક બનાવવી.
words.usage_note: A facilitator guides a group discussion without leading it from a position of authority.
words.memory_tip: 'facilitate' = facil (easy) + itate → make easy → facilitate = સરળ બનાવવું.
examples: She was asked to facilitate the workshop.
A neutral person should facilitate the negotiation.
He facilitated the discussion between the two departments.
Good facilitators keep meetings on track.

words.english_meaning: To formally bring a meeting to an end or to postpone it to another time.
